paragraphs.text: 防止 AI 乱翻文件夹的 DSH 插件 · Path guard for DeepSeek Harness file tools
# 🐟 Prevent-peep
English | 简体中文 | Changelog

> 🐟 When the big fat fish goes wandering, don't let it see what it shouldn't —
> and please don't le

t it upload any of it.
> 😏 Bonus: stops Holy Liang from roasting your XP choices.

A pair of blinkers for **DeepSeek Harness**. Every time the agent wants to touch a
file, it hits a g
ate first — and you decide whether it gets through.
## 🛡️ What it actually does
One window, three lists, four kinds of alert:
| List | Rule |

| ✅ Allow | always let through |
| 🚫 Deny | always questioned (highest priority) |
| 📁 Enforced root
s | only paths under these are policed |

When something trips the gate, mix and match: **🔔 a ding**, **🪟 a silent
corner notification we draw

ourselves**, **💬 the native Windows balloon**, or
**⚠️ a modal you have to click**.

Plus a native folder picker — no typing paths by hand. Changes save themselves and
land within a sec

lder picker — no typing paths by hand. Changes save themselves and
land within a second, no restart.
## ⚠️ Read this: it's a soft lock, not a vault
It stops fat fingers and idle curiosity — not someone who really wants in:

- 🧱 It intercepts **DSH tool calls**, not the operating system
- 🪄 A path assembled inside `pwsh` (`

"D:" + "\secret"`) is invisible to it
- 🚪 Reading the disk outside DSH, using another tool, or just

clicking "allow"
will sail right past it

If you need *nobody* to see it, use **ACLs / an encrypted container / a separate
Windows account** —

that's a real lock. This plugin just makes snooping slightly
more expensive.
## 📦 Install

Requires DSH with a `desktop` or `web` profile. Both packages are needed: `bundle`
is what the plugi
n manager shows, `plugin` is the implementation.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DSH once afterwards 🔄
## 🎛️ Using it

Double-click `plugin/大肥鱼我真该控制你了！.cmd` and poke around. The lists start
empty, so the guard does noth
ing until you pick at least one enforced root.
Settings live in `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\prevent-peep.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Key | Meaning |

| `mode` | `ask` pops the approval card, `deny` fails the call |
| `allowRoots` | always allowed |
|

`denyRoots` | always questioned (highest priority) |
| `enforceRoots` | only paths here are policed

|
| `scanShell` | also scan shell command strings for path-like fragments |
| `relativeBase` | base

for relative paths (falls back to the last `working_directory`) |
| `alertSound` | 🔔 one short ding

|
| `alertCustom` | 🪟 silent self-drawn notification |
| `alertToast` | 💬 native Windows balloon (b

rings its own sound) |
| `alertPopup` | ⚠️ modal confirmation |

Resolution order: **deny → allow → enforced root**. Paths are fully resolved
first (`..`, `\\?\`, `\

\localhost\D$`, `D:foo`, `/` vs `\`, letter case), and on
Windows symlinks / junctions / 8.3 short n

ames are followed too — if either the
literal or the real path is out of bounds, it's out of bounds.
Advanced keys (not in the window, but the window keeps them when you save):
| Key | Default | Meaning |
| `selfProtect` | `true` | non-read-only tools may never write inside `$DSH_HOME` (this plugin's set

tings, DSH's own settings) |
| `protectPluginDir` | `false` | also protect the plugin's code folder.

**Leave off while developing the plugin with DSH** |
| `protectedRoots` | `[]` | extra protected fo

lders |
| `scanScripts` | `true` | when writing `.py` `.ps1` `.js` `.sh` …, scan the written content

for paths. **Noisy when editing this plugin's own tests — turn off temporarily** |
| `suspiciousCom

mands` | `true` | ask before links, new drives, encoded commands, `dsh plugin`, … in the shell |
| `

scanAllArgs` | `true` | search every other argument for absolute paths as a fallback |
| `failClosed

` | `false` | if the guard itself crashes: `false` lets the call through, `true` blocks it |
| `aler

tCooldownMs` | `5000` | minimum gap between alerts, so a looping agent can't flood your screen |
| `

pathKeys` | `file_path`, `path`, `paths`, `workdir`, `cd`, … | arguments treated as a whole path |
|
`scanKeys` | `pattern`, `glob`, `include`, `exclude`, `command` | arguments searched for absolute-p

ath fragments |
| `shellTools` | `pwsh`, `powershell`, `bash`, `sh`, `shell`, `cmd` | tools whose `c

ommand` is governed by `scanShell` |
| `cwdTools` | `working_directory` | tools whose target becomes
the relative-path base |
## 👀 What it watches

Any tool call whose arguments carry a path in `pathKeys`, or an absolute path
inside `scanKeys` — in

practice `read`, `write`, `edit`, `glob` (including the
`pattern`), `grep`, `read_image`, `present`

, `working_directory`, and `pwsh`
(both `workdir` and the command itself). File *contents* you ask i

t to write are
never scanned.
## 🧠 Honest limits

- 🪄 The shell scan is a **heuristic**: common environment variables and `cd`
targets are resolved, b

ut string concatenation (`"D:" + "\x"`), nested
variables, layered `-EncodedCommand`, or a `cd` in o

ne command followed by a
relative path in the next still get past it
- 🔗 Pre-existing **hard links**

and plain **share names** that point back at this
machine can't be traced to their real location
-

📐 Relative paths need a base: `relativeBase`, or the last `working_directory`
the guard saw (shared

across sessions). With neither, they can't be judged
- 🎨 The window background and avatar are crops

of an AI-generated illustration —
swap them out if you redistribute this
